I came with friends on a Monday night so I was very pleasantly surprised to see that the restaurant was buzzy and almost full which all added to the atmospheric ambiance. We sat outside in a very pretty tropical garden setting and the staff were all very helpful and friendly. At first my heart sank at the menu as all of my favourite items were not on there, such as BBQ chicken and pork,deep fried sweet potato, and fried crab and pork spring rolls etc but suddenly I spotted a sauteed chicken dish with bell peppers and and onions. My friend persuaded me to try the chicken and prawn fried spring rolls too and I can honestly say it was the most delicious meal eaten in Vietnam and I have been here for 8 years. Another friend had the thin sauteed beef, lemon grass and chili and it looked equally wonderful so i will definitely ea that next time. We all had garlic rice which was generous and tasted as delicious expected. All of the food was brought out piping hot, none of this indifferent luke warm 'unpleasant temperature food and even the soy sauce and chilies that I asked for was brought well before the food arrived, so that we weren't left waiting whilst the food cooled down. Glasses of wine were a bit on the expensive side compared to other restaurants in Saigon but nothing would be stopping you just having one glass at the restaurant and then going elsewhere to finish off the evening with another glass or two. So I will definitely go again and need to be more adventurous and try other unfamiliar dishes on Quang Bui's menu. Overall, a very pleasant and enjoyable tasty experience with very good service.

Quan Bui, what a beauty!

This was one of the most enjoyable restaurants we visited on our Vietnamese trip. Beautiful setting and decor - as others have said, the interior is like an oasis with a mixed scattering of objects and features - tiles, ceramics, paintings, plants and cute timber furniture. And outside - a lovely garden courtyard. We chose indoors - in May the heat defeated us and we needed the cool of the inside.

The food, drinks and service are wonderful. We went on two consecutive nights, as we had enjoyed it so much. A couple of stand-out dishes: the braised pork, and a skin-on chicken with salad veggies, and most delicious, a plate of pumpkin flowers braised with garlic cloves. This was visually as well as foodishly beautiful. Drinks - a good selection of local craft beers (partner had Te Te) as well as others, and cocktails - I had a lychee and raspberry mojito - wonderful!

The location is in District 2, so not handy if you're staying in District 1, unless by taxi (or speedboat). Great if you are staying at the Villa Song Saigon though (about a 25 minute walk or a few minutes by taxi), or if you are one of the many expats who frequent this district. It's an interesting area, worth a browse.

One final comment: service was excellent, but here's an odd thing. We were very well looked after by a lovely young man on the first night, who went through a few aspects of the food and drinks with us. Then on the second night, he approached us, recognised us and offered to order for us. We smiled and said no, it's OK thanks, we'd like to browse and try ourselves. After that he was distinctly cool, and in fact abandoned us to another (friendly) wait-person. Not sure how we offended him. But that's a small thing - we did love our meals here and would heartily recommend a visit.
